newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian musician Fela charged with drug offences.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian musician Fela charged with drug offences.

text.p: Nigeria's anti-narcotics agency charged Fela Anikulapo-Kuti on Wednesday in court with several drug offences and the maverick musician could face a minimum of 15 years in jail if convicted.
"He has been arraigned today before the tribunal and his offence is standing on many legs, i.e. possession, conspiracy, use which are seperate offences," an agency spokesman said.
Fela, as the 58 year-old musician is widely known, was arrested last week with 107 others at his "The Shrine" nightclub in a working class district of Lagos for alleged possession of cannabis.

He filed a suit at a Lagos court claiming 100 million naira ($11,765) in damages from the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) for alleged violation of his human rights and on Tuesday a judge ordered he should be released by the agency.
But the NDLEA spokesman said Fela was no longer in the custody of the agency. "After being charged the issue is now with the tribunal," he said.
There is no bail for drug offences in Nigeria.
Fela was first arrested last year by NDLEA but later freed.
NDLEA chairman Major-General Musa Bamaiyi told a news conference last week that after Fela's latest arrest his agency had tried to give the musician counselling for his drug habit.
At the same news conference, a handcuffed Fela said what he smoked was "grass" and not drugs.
"I have been smoking for 40 years. It helps my music. People know I smoke worldwide. It is not drugs, it is grass," he said.
The Afro-beat superstar is no stranger to controversy -- or to the jail cell. He has a reputation for openly smoking marijuana and dressing only in his underpants.
Fela was in the past critical of Nigeria's military rulers. Recently he has been a recluse at "The Shrine", occasionally performing in musical shows.
